description: CHATGPT_MODEL_CONTEXT_LENGTHS in sidecar/ai/engines/chatgpt_subscription.py: the entire model catalog is a static id -> context_length dict plus one fallback default, with fixture-owned provenance metadata. There is no dynamic 'GET /models' discovery call in the shipped code despite the original integration plan (§3.2) describing one.

constants.CHATGPT_MODEL_CATALOG_SOURCE: codex rust-v0.146.0 models-manager/models.json + Codex app models_cache.json

notes: The 2026-09-30 catalog (ChatGPT model discovery repair, docs/archive/CHATGPT_MODEL_DISCOVERY_REPAIR.md) adds GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna to the offline fallback at the 272000 conservative default, matching the signed 1.0.4 plugin's provider.json; the 2026-09-07 catalog added GPT-6 Astra at 272000 from the first-party Codex app cache; Spark stays at 128000. This fixture records the engine's static fallback dict, not a frozen descriptor contract: the host-owned authenticated catalog is a request-local overlay that never mutates it. The values are conservative floors: every consumer treats the window as a ceiling, so a value that is too low only compacts earlier while one that is too high causes hard request failures. A value may only be raised from an owner-captured response, with the version bumped in the same edit.

cases.rule: The version stamp is the thing that makes a silent catalog edit detectable; pin it so a value change without a stamp bump fails here too.
Provenance is part of the contract: the numbers are comparison evidence from first-party Codex clients, NOT captured traffic against the private chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex endpoint.
The static fallback catalog is a closed 12-entry dict; an unknown model id resolves to the 272000 default rather than raising or returning zero.
get_model_context_length() is a plain dict lookup on the engine's resolved model slug.
The lookup has a mandatory default row, so a model the catalog has never heard of still gets a usable window.

non_executable.reason: CHATGPT_SUBSCRIPTION_ENGINE_PLAN.md §3.2/§8 describe entitlement-filtered dynamic discovery via an authenticated GET .../codex/models with a bundled fallback catalog. The sidecar still makes no such call: sidecar/ai/engines/catalog.py has discovery helpers for ollama/vllm/openai-compatible and none for chatgpt. Since 2026-09-30 the call is Electron-owned (services/backend/chatgpt-model-catalog-service.js) and reaches the sidecar only as an optional models.list metadata overlay, validated by sidecar/ai/engines/chatgpt_model_catalog.py and applied to a request-local config copy by sidecar/runtime/chatgpt_model_catalog.py; the static dict recorded here remains the fallback. The seam now EXISTS as a documented no-op -- sidecar/runtime/provider_capabilities.py::entitled_chatgpt_models filters the static catalog by an `entitlements` set, and every caller passes entitlements=None, so it returns the catalog unchanged and fails open in both directions. There is nothing to assert about a call that is not made; if the deferred fix ships, it is still expressible declaratively as an endpoint descriptor (GET path, response shape, id/context_length field paths) with the static dict as its fallback.
